index e691aa2..5dfc0a6 100644
--- a/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-1-project-scaffold-stack-integration-core-infrastructure.md
+++ b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-1-project-scaffold-stack-integration-core-infrastructure.md
@@ -76,6 +76,19 @@ context:
 - Given a stubbed response, then only the 6 retryable codes retry; all 14 `Failure` subtypes are reachable.
 - Given the matrix helper run against `auth-signup` for all 3 failure types, then each yields `Left(Failure)`, zero unhandled exceptions, via a reusable API.
 
+### Review Findings
+
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Client-side Dio timeouts (connectTimeout/sendTimeout/receiveTimeout) misclassified as `NETWORK_OFFLINE` instead of `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` [lib/core/network/api_client.dart:103, lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:72] — fixed via shared `dioErrorCodeOf` (`lib/core/network/dio_error_code.dart`), which checks `e.type` before falling back to offline.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Cancelled requests (`DioExceptionType.cancel`) misread as `NETWORK_OFFLINE` and retried by `RetryInterceptor` [lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:72] — fixed in the same shared helper; `cancel` now yields no code, so it's never retried.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] `DioException` → error-code extraction logic duplicated between `ApiClient` and `RetryInterceptor`, risking drift [lib/core/network/api_client.dart:94, lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:67] — unified into `dioErrorCodeOf` (`lib/core/network/dio_error_code.dart`); both files now delegate to it.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] `UrlBuilder.build` only strips a single trailing slash from `baseUrl`, leaving a double slash if `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` has two or more [lib/core/network/url_builder.dart:17] — now strips all trailing slashes via `replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '')`.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf` can throw unguarded inside `onRequest`, hanging the request with no visible error if it does [lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:35] — call site now wrapped in try/catch, falling back to an unrecognized function name and logging via `debugPrint`.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Bootstrap has no error handling for a missing/malformed `.env` — raw crash from `setupCoreDependencies`/`main` instead of a clear setup message [lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:23, lib/main.dart:7] — `main()` now catches, logs a clear "copy .env.example to .env" diagnostic, and rethrows.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Interceptor tests rely on fixed-duration sleeps instead of deterministic synchronization, risking flakiness under load [test/core/network/header_interceptor_test.dart:56, test/core/network/retry_interceptor_test.dart:126] — replaced with `_runOnRequest`/`_runOnError` helpers that await the interceptor's real (void-hidden) Future.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] `ApiClient.get`/`patch`/`delete` have no test coverage — only `post` is exercised [test/core/network/api_client_test.dart:1] — added coverage for all three, including `queryParameters`/`pathParams` pass-through.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] `SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` has no dedicated unit test [lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:19] — added `test/core/network/access_token_provider_test.dart`.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] `HeaderInterceptor` swallows any exception from `readAccessToken()` with a bare `catch (_)` and no logging [lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:42] — now logs via `debugPrint` before proceeding without a token.
+
 ## Spec Change Log

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is a typed stub (Story 1.1), and no shared, reusable UI widgets exist yet; Stories 1.3, 1.5 and 1.6 each need real colors/typography/spacing/radii and a button/text-field/avatar to build against instead of inventing their own.

**Approach:** Implement `design_tokens.dart` verbatim from `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §3, bundle the three prototype type families as static font assets, and build the three cross-feature widgets the epic names as consumed downstream (button variants, text field, avatar) in a new `lib/core/widgets/` location.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Every color/typography/spacing/radius/elevation value in `design_tokens.dart` matches `prototype-extract.md` §3 verbatim; nothing is redefined or hardcoded elsewhere (RNF08).
- Disabled buttons render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text, never dimmed opacity; text fields expose default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
- Every widget honors Dynamic Type — no fixed-height text container that can clip or truncate.
- `core/widgets/` contains only stateless, feature-agnostic presentation primitives — no BLoC, no feature imports, no `data/`/`domain/` coupling (RNF06 applies transitively: these are consumed by every feature's `presentation/`).

**Never:**
- No component outside buttons (primary/secondary-outline/text-ghost), text field, and avatar — every other row in `prototype-extract.md` §6 (chat bubble, insight card, sync badge, filter chip, record card, confirmation dialog, PIN keypad, tab bar, waveform, skeleton, bar chart, persona/kanban cards) ships with the story that first needs it.
- No `google_fonts` runtime-fetch package — fonts are static bundled assets, so widget tests stay deterministic with no device/network (no CI exists yet).
- No extension-feature styling (persona cards, kanban) — out of scope project-wide.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Button disabled | `onPressed == null` | `colorBorder` background, `colorTextSecondary` text, no ripple/pressed feedback | N/A |
| Text field error | `errorText != null` | 1.5px `colorError` border, error text shown below field | N/A |
| Dynamic Type max scale | System text-scale increased | Label wraps/grows; never clips or truncates | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- placeholder stub to replace with real `colors`/`typography`/`spacing`/`radii`/`elevation` constants (currently just a doc comment pointing here).
- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §3 (tokens) and §6 (component table) -- read-only ground truth for every literal value and the exact variations each widget must support.
- `pubspec.yaml` -- add a `fonts:` section + `assets/fonts/` entries for Fraunces, Karla, IBM Plex Mono (no such section exists today; only `.env` is declared as an asset).
- `lib/core/widgets/` -- new directory; architecture spine's Structural Seed is silent on where cross-feature shared widgets live (only `core/design_tokens.dart` is named) — decided here per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed" policy, analogous placement to `core/design_tokens.dart`.
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md` Cross-Story Dependencies -- names exactly this story's output (tokens + buttons/text fields/avatar) as what 1.3/1.5/1.6 consume; do not expand scope beyond it.
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-1-project-scaffold-stack-integration-core-infrastructure.md` Design Notes -- precedent pattern for documenting a decided silent-gap.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- implement real color/typography/spacing/radii/elevation constants verbatim from `prototype-extract.md` §3 -- RNF08 single source of truth
- [x] `assets/fonts/*` + `pubspec.yaml` -- bundle Fraunces/Karla/IBM Plex Mono as static font assets -- deterministic text rendering with no device/CI
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart` -- primary, secondary (outline), text (ghost) variants with the disabled-state rule -- consumed by 1.3/1.5/1.6
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart` -- default/focused/error border states -- consumed by 1.3
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart` -- initials circle, 40px and 52px size variants -- consumed by 1.6 and Epic 8
- [x] `test/core/widgets/app_button_test.dart`, `app_text_field_test.dart`, `avatar_test.dart` -- cover every visual state listed in the I/O matrix and §6
- [x] `test/core/design_tokens_test.dart` -- spot-check token values against `prototype-extract.md` §3

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given any token category, when read from `design_tokens.dart`, then its value matches `prototype-extract.md` §3 verbatim.
- Given a repo-wide search for color/font/spacing/radius literals outside `design_tokens.dart`, then none exist (RNF08).
- Given the disabled button state, when rendered, then background is `colorBorder` and text is `colorTextSecondary`.
- Given the text field error state, when rendered, then the border is 1.5px `colorError`.
- Given increased system Dynamic Type scale, when any of the three widgets render, then no label clips or truncates.

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

Gaps silent in all planning docs, decided here per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed" policy:
- **Shared widget location:** `lib/core/widgets/` — the Structural Seed only names `core/design_tokens.dart`; this is the natural cross-feature home since Clean Architecture already lets `presentation/` depend on `core/`.
- **Font sourcing:** static `.ttf` files committed under `assets/fonts/` and declared in `pubspec.yaml`'s `fonts:` section — not the `google_fonts` package, which fetches at runtime by default and would make widget tests depend on network access with no device/CI yet. Fraunces and Karla ship from Google Fonts only as variable fonts (single file, `wght` axis, no static per-weight instances in the upstream repo); each is declared once per weight actually used by a typography token (`Fraunces-Variable.ttf` at weight 600; `Karla-Variable.ttf` at 400/500/700), which is Flutter's documented pattern for selecting a named instance via `TextStyle.fontWeight` — the files themselves are still fully static/offline, satisfying the "no runtime fetch" intent even though the underlying format is variable. IBM Plex Mono ships its own static `Medium` (500) instance, matching `textMonoCaption` exactly.
- **Epic context's "components" token category:** resolved as a handful of named constants that don't fit color/typography/spacing/radii (avatar sizes 40/52dp, default/focused-or-error border widths 1/1.5dp) — still declared inside `design_tokens.dart`, just grouped for readability.
- **Two colors named in prototype-extract.md §3 but outside its Design Tokens panel** (`colorChatBubbleUser` `#D9DFD3`, `colorCategoryChipText` `#3F4A38`) — added to `design_tokens.dart` now rather than left for whichever later story first renders a chat bubble or category chip, so RNF08 ("nothing is redefined or hardcoded elsewhere") holds from day one instead of being retrofitted.
- **Per-widget `EdgeInsets` constants** (`buttonPadding`, `textFieldContentPadding`, `avatarInitialsPadding`): not named anywhere in `prototype-extract.md` §3, but required so `lib/core/widgets/*.dart` never constructs `EdgeInsets.symmetric/all/only` directly — the Verification section's literal grep (`EdgeInsets\.(all|symmetric|only)(`) checks for the construction call itself, not just raw numbers, so these live in `design_tokens.dart` too, built from the existing spacing scale.
- **Disabled-state uniformity across button variants:** the Boundaries bullet and I/O matrix state the `colorBorder` background / `colorTextSecondary` text disabled rule generically ("Disabled buttons..."), and §6's component table only spells it out for the primary variant. Applied uniformly to all three variants (including secondary-outline and text-ghost, whose disabled state briefly gains a filled `colorBorder` background) for one consistent, testable rule rather than inventing a second disabled treatment for the other two.
- **Avatar vs. the "no fixed-height text container" rule:** the avatar circle is a fixed 40/52dp size by design (a token, not a text-driven container). It wraps its initials in a `FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown)` so at extreme Dynamic Type scales the initials shrink to fit rather than clip or truncate — satisfying the letter of "never clips or truncates" without growing the circle itself.
- **Pressed-state color via `overlayColor`:** `AppButton`'s primary variant resolves `ButtonStyle.overlayColor` to the exact `colorPrimaryPressed` token (opaque) on `WidgetState.pressed`, rather than relying on Material's default semi-transparent overlay tint — keeps the pressed color exact and avoids an unintended "dimmed opacity" look.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves with the new font assets declared, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all new token/widget tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib --include=*.dart | grep -v "core/design_tokens.dart"` -- expected: no matches (RNF08 literal check)

374	+              }

388	+              }
389	+              return Colors.transparent;
390	+            }),

394	+              }
395	+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;

+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// The three button variants named in prototype-extract.md §6's component
+/// table: primary (filled), secondary (outline), text (ghost).
+enum AppButtonVariant { primary, secondaryOutline, textGhost }
+
+/// Shared button primitive consumed by every feature's `presentation/`
+/// (Story 1.3 login/signup, Story 1.5 overlay, Story 1.6 nav shell).
+///
+/// Disabled state is identical across all three variants, per the
+/// project-wide rule: `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary`
+/// text, never a dimmed-opacity look.
+class AppButton extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppButton({
+    super.key,
+    required this.label,
+    required this.onPressed,
+    this.variant = AppButtonVariant.primary,
+    this.textColor,
+  });
+
+  /// Button label. Rendered with no `maxLines`/`overflow` clamp so it
+  /// wraps rather than clips or truncates under Dynamic Type.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Null disables the button and switches it to the disabled visual
+  /// state (see class doc).
+  final VoidCallback? onPressed;
+
+  final AppButtonVariant variant;
+
+  /// Only consulted for [AppButtonVariant.textGhost]: the component table
+  /// allows ghost buttons to use either `colorPrimary` or
+  /// `colorTextSecondary` depending on context (e.g. "Fechar"/"Limpar").
+  /// Defaults to `colorPrimary`.
+  final Color? textColor;
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    final Widget child = Text(label, textAlign: TextAlign.center, style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd);
+
+    final ButtonStyle baseStyle = ButtonStyle(
+      padding: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(DesignTokens.buttonPadding),
+      shape: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(
+        RoundedRectangleBorder(
+          borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+        ),
+      ),
+      elevation: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(0),
+    );
+
+    switch (variant) {
+      case AppButtonVariant.primary:
+        return ElevatedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary;
+            }),
+            overlayColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.pressed)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorPrimaryPressed;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline:
+        return OutlinedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            side: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder);
+              }
+              return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary);
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.textGhost:
+        return TextButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return textColor ?? DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+    }
+  }
+}

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Shared text field primitive (prototype-extract.md §6) with the three
+/// border states the project's boundaries fix: default, focused
+/// (`colorPrimary`, 1.5dp) and error (`colorError`, 1.5dp). Consumed by
+/// Story 1.3's login/signup screen.
+class AppTextField extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppTextField({
+    super.key,
+    this.controller,
+    this.labelText,
+    this.hintText,
+    this.errorText,
+    this.obscureText = false,
+    this.keyboardType,
+    this.textInputAction,
+    this.onChanged,
+    this.focusNode,
+    this.maxLines = 1,
+  });
+
+  final TextEditingController? controller;
+  final String? labelText;
+  final String? hintText;
+
+  /// Non-null (and non-empty) switches the field to the error border
+  /// state and shows this text below the field.
+  final String? errorText;
+
+  final bool obscureText;
+  final TextInputType? keyboardType;
+  final TextInputAction? textInputAction;
+  final ValueChanged<String>? onChanged;
+  final FocusNode? focusNode;
+
+  /// `null` allows unlimited lines (e.g. the insertion modal's "Texto"
+  /// tab); defaults to a single line for form fields like login.
+  final int? maxLines;
+
+  OutlineInputBorder _border(Color color, double width) {
+    return OutlineInputBorder(
+      borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+      borderSide: BorderSide(color: color, width: width),
+    );
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return TextField(
+      controller: controller,
+      focusNode: focusNode,
+      obscureText: obscureText,
+      keyboardType: keyboardType,
+      textInputAction: textInputAction,
+      onChanged: onChanged,
+      maxLines: obscureText ? 1 : maxLines,
+      minLines: null,
+      style: DesignTokens.textBodyLg.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary),
+      cursorColor: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+      decoration: InputDecoration(
+        labelText: labelText,
+        hintText: hintText,
+        errorText: errorText,
+        // Unbounded so a long error message wraps instead of being
+        // truncated under Dynamic Type.
+        errorMaxLines: null,
+        filled: true,
+        fillColor: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
+        contentPadding: DesignTokens.textFieldContentPadding,
+        labelStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        hintStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        errorStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorError),
+        border: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        enabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        focusedBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorPrimary, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        errorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        focusedErrorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        disabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Initials avatar (prototype-extract.md §6): a solid `colorPrimary`
+/// circle with 1–2 uppercase initials, in two sizes — 40dp in the side
+/// menu (Story 1.6), 52dp in Configurações (Epic 8).
+class Avatar extends StatelessWidget {
+  const Avatar({super.key, required this.initials, this.size = AvatarSize.small});
+
+  /// Expected to be 1–2 characters; rendered as given (uppercased) with
+  /// no truncation enforced here — the caller owns deriving initials
+  /// from a name.
+  final String initials;
+
+  final AvatarSize size;
+
+  double get _diameter {
+    switch (size) {
+      case AvatarSize.small:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm;
+      case AvatarSize.large:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeLg;
+    }
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return Container(
+      width: _diameter,
+      height: _diameter,
+      alignment: Alignment.center,
+      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
+        color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+        shape: BoxShape.circle,
+      ),
+      // The circle is a fixed design-token size (not a text container
+      // sized to its content); FittedBox shrinks the initials to fit
+      // under extreme Dynamic Type scales instead of clipping/truncating.
+      child: FittedBox(
+        fit: BoxFit.scaleDown,
+        child: Padding(
+          padding: DesignTokens.avatarInitialsPadding,
+          child: Text(
+            initials.toUpperCase(),
+            style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary),
+            maxLines: 1,
+            softWrap: false,
+          ),
+        ),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}
+
+enum AvatarSize { small, large }

1	# Verification Gap Review
2	
3	**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.
4	
5	The main verification gap shapes are:
6	
7	1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
8	2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
9	3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.
10	
11	## Evidence Rules
12	
13	- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
14	- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
15	- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
16	- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
17	- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.
18	
19	## Review Sequence
20	
21	### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change
22	
23	Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.
24	
25	Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.
26	
27	Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.
28	
29	If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).
30	
31	### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed
32	
33	Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.
34	
35	Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.
36	
37	### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used
38	
39	Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.
40	
41	Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.
42	
43	### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test
44	
45	For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.
46	
47	A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.
48	
49	Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.
50	
51	- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
52	- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
53	- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.
54	
55	A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.
56	
57	For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.
58	
59	Common patterns:
60	
61	- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
62	- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
63	- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
64	- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
65	- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
66	- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.
67	
68	### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real
69	
70	Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.
71	
72	Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.
73	
74	Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.
75	
76	Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.
77	
78	## OUTPUT FORMAT
79	
80	Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.
81	
82	```markdown
83	### <one-line title naming the gap>
84	
85	- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
86	- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
87	- **Existing test evidence:**
88	  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
89	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
90	  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
91	- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
92	- **Demonstration:**
93	  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
94	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
95	- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
96	- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
97	```
98	
99	If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:
100	
101	```markdown
102	## Other findings
103	
104	- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
105	```
106	
107	When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:
108	
109	`No verification gaps found.`
110	
111	## CONTENT SOURCE
112	
113	Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`
114

A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.

Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.

- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.

A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.

For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns:

- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.

### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real

Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.

Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.

Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.

Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.

```markdown
### <one-line title naming the gap>

- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
- **Existing test evidence:**
  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
- **Demonstration:**
  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
```

If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:

```markdown
## Other findings

- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
```

When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:

`No verification gaps found.`

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// The three button variants named in prototype-extract.md §6's component
+/// table: primary (filled), secondary (outline), text (ghost).
+enum AppButtonVariant { primary, secondaryOutline, textGhost }
+
+/// Shared button primitive consumed by every feature's `presentation/`
+/// (Story 1.3 login/signup, Story 1.5 overlay, Story 1.6 nav shell).
+///
+/// Disabled state is identical across all three variants, per the
+/// project-wide rule: `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary`
+/// text, never a dimmed-opacity look.
+class AppButton extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppButton({
+    super.key,
+    required this.label,
+    required this.onPressed,
+    this.variant = AppButtonVariant.primary,
+    this.textColor,
+  });
+
+  /// Button label. Rendered with no `maxLines`/`overflow` clamp so it
+  /// wraps rather than clips or truncates under Dynamic Type.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Null disables the button and switches it to the disabled visual
+  /// state (see class doc).
+  final VoidCallback? onPressed;
+
+  final AppButtonVariant variant;
+
+  /// Only consulted for [AppButtonVariant.textGhost]: the component table
+  /// allows ghost buttons to use either `colorPrimary` or
+  /// `colorTextSecondary` depending on context (e.g. "Fechar"/"Limpar").
+  /// Defaults to `colorPrimary`.
+  final Color? textColor;
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    final Widget child = Text(label, textAlign: TextAlign.center, style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd);
+
+    final ButtonStyle baseStyle = ButtonStyle(
+      padding: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(DesignTokens.buttonPadding),
+      shape: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(
+        RoundedRectangleBorder(
+          borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+        ),
+      ),
+      elevation: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(0),
+    );
+
+    switch (variant) {
+      case AppButtonVariant.primary:
+        return ElevatedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary;
+            }),
+            overlayColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.pressed)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorPrimaryPressed;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline:
+        return OutlinedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            side: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder);
+              }
+              return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary);
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.textGhost:
+        return TextButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return textColor ?? DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );

+    this.obscureText = false,

+    this.onChanged,

+    this.maxLines = 1,
+  });
+
+  final TextEditingController? controller;
+  final String? labelText;
+  final String? hintText;
+
+  /// Non-null (and non-empty) switches the field to the error border
+  /// state and shows this text below the field.

+
+  final bool obscureText;
+  final TextInputType? keyboardType;
+  final TextInputAction? textInputAction;

+    return OutlineInputBorder(
+      borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+      borderSide: BorderSide(color: color, width: width),

+    return TextField(

+      focusNode: focusNode,
+      obscureText: obscureText,
+      keyboardType: keyboardType,
+      textInputAction: textInputAction,
+      onChanged: onChanged,
+      maxLines: obscureText ? 1 : maxLines,
+      minLines: null,

+      cursorColor: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// The three button variants named in prototype-extract.md §6's component
+/// table: primary (filled), secondary (outline), text (ghost).
+enum AppButtonVariant { primary, secondaryOutline, textGhost }
+
+/// Shared button primitive consumed by every feature's `presentation/`
+/// (Story 1.3 login/signup, Story 1.5 overlay, Story 1.6 nav shell).
+///
+/// Disabled state is identical across all three variants, per the
+/// project-wide rule: `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary`
+/// text, never a dimmed-opacity look.
+class AppButton extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppButton({
+    super.key,
+    required this.label,
+    required this.onPressed,
+    this.variant = AppButtonVariant.primary,
+    this.textColor,
+  });
+
+  /// Button label. Rendered with no `maxLines`/`overflow` clamp so it
+  /// wraps rather than clips or truncates under Dynamic Type.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Null disables the button and switches it to the disabled visual
+  /// state (see class doc).
+  final VoidCallback? onPressed;
+
+  final AppButtonVariant variant;
+
+  /// Only consulted for [AppButtonVariant.textGhost]: the component table
+  /// allows ghost buttons to use either `colorPrimary` or
+  /// `colorTextSecondary` depending on context (e.g. "Fechar"/"Limpar").
+  /// Defaults to `colorPrimary`.
+  final Color? textColor;
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    final Widget child = Text(label, textAlign: TextAlign.center, style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd);
+
+    final ButtonStyle baseStyle = ButtonStyle(
+      padding: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(DesignTokens.buttonPadding),
+      shape: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(
+        RoundedRectangleBorder(
+          borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+        ),
+      ),
+      elevation: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(0),
+    );
+
+    switch (variant) {
+      case AppButtonVariant.primary:
+        return ElevatedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary;
+            }),
+            overlayColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.pressed)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorPrimaryPressed;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline:
+        return OutlinedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            side: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder);
+              }
+              return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary);
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.textGhost:
+        return TextButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return textColor ?? DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+    }
+  }
+}

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Shared text field primitive (prototype-extract.md §6) with the three
+/// border states the project's boundaries fix: default, focused
+/// (`colorPrimary`, 1.5dp) and error (`colorError`, 1.5dp). Consumed by
+/// Story 1.3's login/signup screen.
+class AppTextField extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppTextField({
+    super.key,
+    this.controller,
+    this.labelText,
+    this.hintText,
+    this.errorText,
+    this.obscureText = false,
+    this.keyboardType,
+    this.textInputAction,
+    this.onChanged,
+    this.focusNode,
+    this.maxLines = 1,
+  });
+
+  final TextEditingController? controller;
+  final String? labelText;
+  final String? hintText;
+
+  /// Non-null (and non-empty) switches the field to the error border
+  /// state and shows this text below the field.
+  final String? errorText;
+
+  final bool obscureText;
+  final TextInputType? keyboardType;
+  final TextInputAction? textInputAction;
+  final ValueChanged<String>? onChanged;
+  final FocusNode? focusNode;
+
+  /// `null` allows unlimited lines (e.g. the insertion modal's "Texto"
+  /// tab); defaults to a single line for form fields like login.
+  final int? maxLines;
+
+  OutlineInputBorder _border(Color color, double width) {
+    return OutlineInputBorder(
+      borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+      borderSide: BorderSide(color: color, width: width),
+    );
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return TextField(
+      controller: controller,
+      focusNode: focusNode,
+      obscureText: obscureText,
+      keyboardType: keyboardType,
+      textInputAction: textInputAction,
+      onChanged: onChanged,
+      maxLines: obscureText ? 1 : maxLines,
+      minLines: null,
+      style: DesignTokens.textBodyLg.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary),
+      cursorColor: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+      decoration: InputDecoration(
+        labelText: labelText,
+        hintText: hintText,
+        errorText: errorText,
+        // Unbounded so a long error message wraps instead of being
+        // truncated under Dynamic Type.
+        errorMaxLines: null,
+        filled: true,
+        fillColor: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
+        contentPadding: DesignTokens.textFieldContentPadding,
+        labelStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        hintStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        errorStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorError),
+        border: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        enabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        focusedBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorPrimary, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        errorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        focusedErrorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        disabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Initials avatar (prototype-extract.md §6): a solid `colorPrimary`
+/// circle with 1–2 uppercase initials, in two sizes — 40dp in the side
+/// menu (Story 1.6), 52dp in Configurações (Epic 8).
+class Avatar extends StatelessWidget {
+  const Avatar({super.key, required this.initials, this.size = AvatarSize.small});
+
+  /// Expected to be 1–2 characters; rendered as given (uppercased) with
+  /// no truncation enforced here — the caller owns deriving initials
+  /// from a name.
+  final String initials;
+
+  final AvatarSize size;
+
+  double get _diameter {
+    switch (size) {
+      case AvatarSize.small:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm;
+      case AvatarSize.large:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeLg;
+    }
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return Container(
+      width: _diameter,
+      height: _diameter,
+      alignment: Alignment.center,
+      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
+        color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+        shape: BoxShape.circle,
+      ),
+      // The circle is a fixed design-token size (not a text container
+      // sized to its content); FittedBox shrinks the initials to fit
+      // under extreme Dynamic Type scales instead of clipping/truncating.
+      child: FittedBox(
+        fit: BoxFit.scaleDown,
+        child: Padding(
+          padding: DesignTokens.avatarInitialsPadding,
+          child: Text(
+            initials.toUpperCase(),
+            style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary),
+            maxLines: 1,
+            softWrap: false,
+          ),
+        ),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}
+
+enum AvatarSize { small, large }

+  final VoidCallback? onPressed;
+
+  final AppButtonVariant variant;
+
+  /// Only consulted for [AppButtonVariant.textGhost]: the component table
+  /// allows ghost buttons to use either `colorPrimary` or
+  /// `colorTextSecondary` depending on context (e.g. "Fechar"/"Limpar").
+  /// Defaults to `colorPrimary`.
+  final Color? textColor;
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    final Widget child = Text(label, textAlign: TextAlign.center, style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd);
+
+    final ButtonStyle baseStyle = ButtonStyle(
+      padding: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(DesignTokens.buttonPadding),
+      shape: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(
+        RoundedRectangleBorder(
+          borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+        ),
+      ),
+      elevation: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(0),
+    );
+
+    switch (variant) {
+      case AppButtonVariant.primary:
+        return ElevatedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary;
+            }),
+            overlayColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.pressed)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorPrimaryPressed;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline:
+        return OutlinedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            side: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder);
+              }
+              return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary);
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.textGhost:
+        return TextButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return textColor ?? DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+    }
+  }

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Shared text field primitive (prototype-extract.md §6) with the three
+/// border states the project's boundaries fix: default, focused
+/// (`colorPrimary`, 1.5dp) and error (`colorError`, 1.5dp). Consumed by
+/// Story 1.3's login/signup screen.
+class AppTextField extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppTextField({
+    super.key,
+    this.controller,
+    this.labelText,
+    this.hintText,
+    this.errorText,
+    this.obscureText = false,
+    this.keyboardType,
+    this.textInputAction,
+    this.onChanged,
+    this.focusNode,
+    this.maxLines = 1,
+  });
+
+  final TextEditingController? controller;
+  final String? labelText;
+  final String? hintText;
+
+  /// Non-null (and non-empty) switches the field to the error border
+  /// state and shows this text below the field.
+  final String? errorText;
+
+  final bool obscureText;
+  final TextInputType? keyboardType;
+  final TextInputAction? textInputAction;
+  final ValueChanged<String>? onChanged;
+  final FocusNode? focusNode;
+
+  /// `null` allows unlimited lines (e.g. the insertion modal's "Texto"
+  /// tab); defaults to a single line for form fields like login.
+  final int? maxLines;
+
+  OutlineInputBorder _border(Color color, double width) {
+    return OutlineInputBorder(
+      borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+      borderSide: BorderSide(color: color, width: width),
+    );
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return TextField(
+      controller: controller,
+      focusNode: focusNode,
+      obscureText: obscureText,
+      keyboardType: keyboardType,
+      textInputAction: textInputAction,
+      onChanged: onChanged,
+      maxLines: obscureText ? 1 : maxLines,
+      minLines: null,
+      style: DesignTokens.textBodyLg.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary),
+      cursorColor: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+      decoration: InputDecoration(
+        labelText: labelText,
+        hintText: hintText,
+        errorText: errorText,
+        // Unbounded so a long error message wraps instead of being
+        // truncated under Dynamic Type.
+        errorMaxLines: null,
+        filled: true,
+        fillColor: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
+        contentPadding: DesignTokens.textFieldContentPadding,
+        labelStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        hintStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        errorStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorError),
+        border: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        enabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        focusedBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorPrimary, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        errorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        focusedErrorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        disabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Initials avatar (prototype-extract.md §6): a solid `colorPrimary`
+/// circle with 1–2 uppercase initials, in two sizes — 40dp in the side
+/// menu (Story 1.6), 52dp in Configurações (Epic 8).
+class Avatar extends StatelessWidget {
+  const Avatar({super.key, required this.initials, this.size = AvatarSize.small});
+
+  /// Expected to be 1–2 characters; rendered as given (uppercased) with
+  /// no truncation enforced here — the caller owns deriving initials
+  /// from a name.
+  final String initials;
+
+  final AvatarSize size;
+
+  double get _diameter {
+    switch (size) {
+      case AvatarSize.small:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm;
+      case AvatarSize.large:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeLg;
+    }
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return Container(
+      width: _diameter,
+      height: _diameter,
+      alignment: Alignment.center,
+      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
+        color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+        shape: BoxShape.circle,
+      ),
+      // The circle is a fixed design-token size (not a text container
+      // sized to its content); FittedBox shrinks the initials to fit
+      // under extreme Dynamic Type scales instead of clipping/truncating.
+      child: FittedBox(
+        fit: BoxFit.scaleDown,
+        child: Padding(
+          padding: DesignTokens.avatarInitialsPadding,
+          child: Text(
+            initials.toUpperCase(),
+            style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary),
+            maxLines: 1,
+            softWrap: false,
+          ),
+        ),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}
+
+enum AvatarSize { small, large }

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// The three button variants named in prototype-extract.md §6's component
+/// table: primary (filled), secondary (outline), text (ghost).
+enum AppButtonVariant { primary, secondaryOutline, textGhost }
+
+/// Shared button primitive consumed by every feature's `presentation/`
+/// (Story 1.3 login/signup, Story 1.5 overlay, Story 1.6 nav shell).
+///
+/// Disabled state is identical across all three variants, per the
+/// project-wide rule: `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary`
+/// text, never a dimmed-opacity look.
+class AppButton extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppButton({
+    super.key,
+    required this.label,
+    required this.onPressed,
+    this.variant = AppButtonVariant.primary,
+    this.textColor,
+  });
+
+  /// Button label. Rendered with no `maxLines`/`overflow` clamp so it
+  /// wraps rather than clips or truncates under Dynamic Type.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Null disables the button and switches it to the disabled visual
+  /// state (see class doc).
+  final VoidCallback? onPressed;
+
+  final AppButtonVariant variant;
+
+  /// Only consulted for [AppButtonVariant.textGhost]: the component table
+  /// allows ghost buttons to use either `colorPrimary` or
+  /// `colorTextSecondary` depending on context (e.g. "Fechar"/"Limpar").
+  /// Defaults to `colorPrimary`.
+  final Color? textColor;
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    final Widget child = Text(label, textAlign: TextAlign.center, style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd);
+
+    final ButtonStyle baseStyle = ButtonStyle(
+      padding: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(DesignTokens.buttonPadding),
+      shape: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(
+        RoundedRectangleBorder(
+          borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+        ),
+      ),
+      elevation: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(0),
+    );
+
+    switch (variant) {
+      case AppButtonVariant.primary:
+        return ElevatedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary;
+            }),
+            overlayColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.pressed)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorPrimaryPressed;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline:
+        return OutlinedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            side: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder);
+              }
+              return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary);
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,

+
+      case AppButtonVariant.textGhost:
+        return TextButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return textColor ?? DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// The three button variants named in prototype-extract.md §6's component
+/// table: primary (filled), secondary (outline), text (ghost).
+enum AppButtonVariant { primary, secondaryOutline, textGhost }
+
+/// Shared button primitive consumed by every feature's `presentation/`
+/// (Story 1.3 login/signup, Story 1.5 overlay, Story 1.6 nav shell).
+///
+/// Disabled state is identical across all three variants, per the
+/// project-wide rule: `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary`
+/// text, never a dimmed-opacity look.
+class AppButton extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppButton({
+    super.key,
+    required this.label,
+    required this.onPressed,
+    this.variant = AppButtonVariant.primary,
+    this.textColor,
+  });
+
+  /// Button label. Rendered with no `maxLines`/`overflow` clamp so it
+  /// wraps rather than clips or truncates under Dynamic Type.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Null disables the button and switches it to the disabled visual
+  /// state (see class doc).
+  final VoidCallback? onPressed;
+
+  final AppButtonVariant variant;
+
+  /// Only consulted for [AppButtonVariant.textGhost]: the component table
+  /// allows ghost buttons to use either `colorPrimary` or
+  /// `colorTextSecondary` depending on context (e.g. "Fechar"/"Limpar").
+  /// Defaults to `colorPrimary`.
+  final Color? textColor;
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    final Widget child = Text(label, textAlign: TextAlign.center, style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd);
+
+    final ButtonStyle baseStyle = ButtonStyle(
+      padding: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(DesignTokens.buttonPadding),
+      shape: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(
+        RoundedRectangleBorder(
+          borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+        ),
+      ),
+      elevation: const WidgetStatePropertyAll(0),
+    );
+
+    switch (variant) {
+      case AppButtonVariant.primary:
+        return ElevatedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary;
+            }),
+            overlayColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.pressed)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorPrimaryPressed;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline:
+        return OutlinedButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+            side: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder);
+              }
+              return const BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary);
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+
+      case AppButtonVariant.textGhost:
+        return TextButton(
+          onPressed: onPressed,
+          style: baseStyle.copyWith(
+            backgroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorBorder;
+              }
+              return Colors.transparent;
+            }),
+            foregroundColor: WidgetStateProperty.resolveWith((states) {
+              if (states.contains(WidgetState.disabled)) {
+                return DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary;
+              }
+              return textColor ?? DesignTokens.colorPrimary;
+            }),
+          ),
+          child: child,
+        );
+    }
+  }
+}

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Shared text field primitive (prototype-extract.md §6) with the three
+/// border states the project's boundaries fix: default, focused
+/// (`colorPrimary`, 1.5dp) and error (`colorError`, 1.5dp). Consumed by
+/// Story 1.3's login/signup screen.
+class AppTextField extends StatelessWidget {
+  const AppTextField({
+    super.key,
+    this.controller,
+    this.labelText,
+    this.hintText,
+    this.errorText,
+    this.obscureText = false,
+    this.keyboardType,
+    this.textInputAction,
+    this.onChanged,
+    this.focusNode,
+    this.maxLines = 1,
+  });
+
+  final TextEditingController? controller;
+  final String? labelText;
+  final String? hintText;
+
+  /// Non-null (and non-empty) switches the field to the error border
+  /// state and shows this text below the field.
+  final String? errorText;
+
+  final bool obscureText;
+  final TextInputType? keyboardType;
+  final TextInputAction? textInputAction;
+  final ValueChanged<String>? onChanged;
+  final FocusNode? focusNode;
+
+  /// `null` allows unlimited lines (e.g. the insertion modal's "Texto"
+  /// tab); defaults to a single line for form fields like login.
+  final int? maxLines;
+
+  OutlineInputBorder _border(Color color, double width) {
+    return OutlineInputBorder(
+      borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm)),
+      borderSide: BorderSide(color: color, width: width),
+    );
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return TextField(
+      controller: controller,
+      focusNode: focusNode,
+      obscureText: obscureText,
+      keyboardType: keyboardType,
+      textInputAction: textInputAction,
+      onChanged: onChanged,
+      maxLines: obscureText ? 1 : maxLines,
+      minLines: null,
+      style: DesignTokens.textBodyLg.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary),
+      cursorColor: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+      decoration: InputDecoration(
+        labelText: labelText,
+        hintText: hintText,
+        errorText: errorText,
+        // Unbounded so a long error message wraps instead of being
+        // truncated under Dynamic Type.
+        errorMaxLines: null,
+        filled: true,
+        fillColor: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
+        contentPadding: DesignTokens.textFieldContentPadding,
+        labelStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        hintStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary),
+        errorStyle: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorError),
+        border: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        enabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+        focusedBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorPrimary, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        errorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        focusedErrorBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorError, DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis),
+        disabledBorder: _border(DesignTokens.colorBorder, DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}

+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Initials avatar (prototype-extract.md §6): a solid `colorPrimary`
+/// circle with 1–2 uppercase initials, in two sizes — 40dp in the side
+/// menu (Story 1.6), 52dp in Configurações (Epic 8).
+class Avatar extends StatelessWidget {
+  const Avatar({super.key, required this.initials, this.size = AvatarSize.small});
+
+  /// Expected to be 1–2 characters; rendered as given (uppercased) with
+  /// no truncation enforced here — the caller owns deriving initials
+  /// from a name.
+  final String initials;
+
+  final AvatarSize size;
+
+  double get _diameter {
+    switch (size) {
+      case AvatarSize.small:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm;
+      case AvatarSize.large:
+        return DesignTokens.avatarSizeLg;
+    }
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return Container(
+      width: _diameter,
+      height: _diameter,
+      alignment: Alignment.center,
+      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
+        color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+        shape: BoxShape.circle,
+      ),
+      // The circle is a fixed design-token size (not a text container
+      // sized to its content); FittedBox shrinks the initials to fit
+      // under extreme Dynamic Type scales instead of clipping/truncating.
+      child: FittedBox(
+        fit: BoxFit.scaleDown,
+        child: Padding(
+          padding: DesignTokens.avatarInitialsPadding,
+          child: Text(
+            initials.toUpperCase(),
+            style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorOnPrimary),
+            maxLines: 1,
+            softWrap: false,
+          ),
+        ),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}
+
+enum AvatarSize { small, large }

+  );
+}

+    expect(tester.getSize(find.byType(Container)), const Size(DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm, DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm));
+
+    final decoration = container.decoration as BoxDecoration;
+    expect(decoration.color, DesignTokens.colorPrimary);
+    expect(decoration.shape, BoxShape.circle);
+
+    expect(find.text('WD'), findsOneWidget);
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('large variant renders a 52dp circle', (tester) async {
+    await tester.pumpWidget(_wrap(const Avatar(initials: 'AM', size: AvatarSize.large)));
+
+    expect(tester.getSize(find.byType(Container)), const Size(DesignTokens.avatarSizeLg, DesignTokens.avatarSizeLg));
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('uppercases lowercase initials', (tester) async {
+    await tester.pumpWidget(_wrap(const Avatar(initials: 'wd')));
+
+    expect(find.text('WD'), findsOneWidget);
+    expect(find.text('wd'), findsNothing);
+  });
+
+  testWidgets('initials never clip or truncate under a large Dynamic Type scale', (tester) async {
+    await tester.pumpWidget(_wrap(const Avatar(initials: 'WD'), textScale: 3.0));
+    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+
+    expect(tester.takeException(), isNull);
+
+    // The circle itself stays fixed-size (it's a design-token, not a
+    // text-driven container); FittedBox is what prevents clipping by
+    // shrinking the initials to fit instead.
+    expect(tester.getSize(find.byType(Container)), const Size(DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm, DesignTokens.avatarSizeSm));
+    expect(find.byType(FittedBox), findsOneWidget);
+

+/// table: primary (filled), secondary (outline), text (ghost).
